title: Sell Mineral Rights in Kimberly, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kimberly, AL | Offer
metaDescription: Kimberly, AL mineral owner in the Black Warrior coalbed methane fairway? Get a clear cash offer based on your actual royalty history.
heroLead: Kimberly is a small city on the northern edge of Jefferson County, close to the Warrior River and inside a stretch of the basin where coal and gas leasing overlap heavily in the local land records.
intro: We buy interests from Kimberly owners fairly regularly, usually small fractional shares tied to family farms that were leased for coalbed methane development years ago. If that describes your situation, you likely already have a royalty statement sitting somewhere that tells us most of what we need to know.

sections.heading: Reading the statement you already have
paragraphs: A typical Kimberly-area statement lists the well or unit name, your interest type, usually a royalty interest rather than a working interest, your decimal share, gross production volume, and the net amount paid after deductions. If any of that is confusing, we are happy to walk through it with you over the phone before you decide anything.
The decimal interest line is the single most important number on the page for valuation purposes, so start there if you want a quick sense of scale.

sections.heading: Why some Kimberly families choose to sell now
paragraphs: Coalbed methane wells in this stretch of the basin were largely drilled some years back, so most are well into their production decline. For owners who want to fund a specific goal, help a grandchild with school, pay down a mortgage, consolidate scattered small assets, converting the remaining royalty stream into one payment can make more practical sense than years of small deposits.
We lay out both paths honestly: what a lump sum looks like today, and roughly what continuing to hold might pay out over time, so you can weigh it yourself.

faqs.question: What operator typically runs the wells near Kimberly?
faqs.answer: Diversified Energy operates a large share of the legacy coalbed methane wells in this part of the basin, following its acquisition of Energen's assets.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests with multiple heirs listed?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can work with each heir separately or coordinate one purchase covering the whole family's combined interest.

faqs.question: How does a coalbed methane royalty differ from a regular oil royalty?
faqs.answer: The underlying economics are similar, a decimal share of production revenue, but coalbed methane wells tend to decline more gradually and produce for longer at lower volumes.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum size interest you will buy?
faqs.answer: Not really, we evaluate even small fractional interests, though very small ones may take a bit more time to research before we can quote.
